title: Day, Night & Seasons: The Tilt
welcome_lead: Earth's tilt — not its distance — gives us the four seasons.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: 23.5° tilt causes seasons, solstice, equinox.
final_note: Tilt is the secret behind your favourite (or worst) season.

concepts.def: Longest or shortest day of the year.

walkthroughs.body_html: Earth's axis is tilted by about 23.5°. This tilt means each hemisphere leans toward the Sun for half the year and away for the other half.
When your hemisphere tilts toward the Sun you get longer days, higher Sun and warmer weather — summer. The opposite gives winter.
The longest day in the UK is around 21 June (summer solstice). The shortest is around 21 December. Equinoxes split day and night equally.
